title: Capture-path probe — what capture is possible on 22.0.368, and what it costs
status_note: Describes what happened (Law 3). All four brief questions were answered against the live build by eleven Karma renders and seven live-introspection producers, every one of which is left in the tree as a runnable script beside the JSON it emits. The ID-AOV gate was answered NEGATIVE on three independent grounds. NO capture code, NO cv2 code, NO V2 controls were written; NO source outside harness/notes/ was touched. Two results contradicted my own first pass and were corrected in-run and recorded rather than quietly fixed: the Copernicus content check returned INCONCLUSIVE before it returned CONFIRMED, and a resolutiony parm set was refused and reported rather than assumed. The scoped-delta primitive remains BLOCKED — this leg learned what is true, it did not change what is true.
settings_profile: harness/readonly-settings.json (governing). RECORDED HONESTLY, NOT CLAIMED: execution was an interactive Claude Code session whose grant is wider than that file. The fence was self-enforced — every write went to harness/notes/**; render outputs went to the session scratchpad OUTSIDE the repo so no binaries entered the tree. No subagents were dispatched; all probes were run directly so the raw output was seen unfiltered.
commit_at_run: STARTED 2105453 (feat/repair-heats-01) — ENDED 6983c73 (docs/how-we-know). The shared checkout was re-pointed by a concurrent leg mid-run; see drift D2. All runtime findings are unaffected; the one static finding was re-verified at 6983c73.
worktree: NONE. legs.json declares .claude/worktrees/v1-capture-probe; that directory is empty and is not a registered git worktree, so this leg ran against the shared main checkout. See drift D2.

rulings.R50: ABSENT requires a positive control ON THE SAME CLASS; where no control is possible the verdict is UNVERIFIABLE, never ABSENT. Applied to every ABSENT verdict below — each cites a same-class full dir() member count plus sibling spellings resolving in the same run.
rulings.R58: Read the COMPLETE method list rather than keyword-searching. Applied as method: full dir() dumps per class, then an exhaustive 530-class sweep of the hou namespace.
rulings.R73: A verified NARROW claim does not license a BROAD sentence. Applied twice — the namespace sweep before any 'no viewport-grab API exists' statement, and the primid-only control render before the retina/ingest.py defect was stated.
rulings.R90: Wrong spellings with live call sites are actionable. Applied to the R102 control-list correction (V1-F8) and the retina/ingest.py selection defect (V1-F9).
rulings.R25: Receipt records model + settings_profile. Both above.
rulings.R92: Declare touches so collisions are detectable before dispatch. This leg touches harness/notes/** only.
rulings.R93: as amended by R103 — a read-only leg's product IS its receipt; the fence denies git commit and the fence wins.

suite.note: NOT RUN and NOT CLAIMED. harness/readonly-settings.json carries no pytest allow; Constitution Article V says a leg under a profile without pytest cannot claim suite evidence. This leg changed no product code, so the suite is not the instrument that would detect its effect.

headline: Capture works, is deterministic, and costs ~2.4 s flat in resolution. The MASK does not exist: Karma 22.0.368 supplies no per-object integer ID on any path probed. Step 4 of the RETINA claim has no supplier on this renderer. One candidate remains un-probed (cryptomatte) and one new direction is well-evidenced (Copernicus Int32 readback at 2.4 ms).

findings.claim: No usable per-object integer ID mask exists on Karma 22.0.368 via any path probed. The scoped-delta primitive cannot be built as designed.
findings.anchor: Three independent grounds, all in v1_q2_analysis.json + v1_q2_parmdetail.json: (1) primidprecision/elementprecision menus are exactly ['half','float'] — no integer option exists at the parm surface; (2) an int32 render-var format is refused at render; (3) neither primid, element nor ray:objectid separates two disjoint spheres.
findings.reproduces: R100 / V1-F1 (prior run, evidence absent from tree)

findings.claim: primid is a PER-POLYGON id whose range is reused by every object. It is not an object identifier and using it as one produces masks that are confidently wrong.
findings.anchor: v1_q2_analysis.json files.base.analysis.subimages[2].separation — sampling boxes well inside each sphere: left 180 distinct, right 184 distinct, 123 SHARED. element likewise: 413 / 401 / 89 shared. ray:objectid: 6 / 7 / 6 shared. Producer v1_q2_analyse.py.
findings.reproduces: R100 / V1-F2 (counts differ — different scene and resolution; finding identical)

findings.claim: The ID AOV is float BY CONSTRUCTION, visible without rendering: karmarendersettings.primidprecision and .elementprecision are menus with exactly two entries, ['half','float'], default 'float'.
findings.anchor: v1_q2_parmdetail.json karmarendersettings.primidprecision.menu_items. Producer v1_q2_parmdetail.py. Emitted EXR channel format confirms it: primid.id and element.id are 'float'; beauty C is 'half' (v1_q2_analysis.json channelformats).

findings.claim: Karma refuses an integer render-var format outright. The render fails; no output is produced.
findings.anchor: v1_q2_render.json cases.int_format — husk log: "Unsupported image data format 'int32' in RenderVar /Render/Products/Vars/int_objectid" then "Error defining render products"; hou raises OperationFailed, exit code 1, output_exists=false. Producer v1_q2_render.py.

findings.claim: The ray: namespace prefix is REQUIRED on a custom render-var sourceName. A bare name emits a correctly-named, correctly-shaped EXR part FILLED WITH ZEROS, SILENTLY — no error, no warning. Any pipeline reading that part gets zeros and has no way to know it asked wrong.
findings.anchor: v1_q2_analysis.json files.bare_names vs files.ray_names. Same-frame positive control: in ONE render, bare 'objectid' and bare 'primid' are all_zero=true (1 distinct value), while ray:primid carries real data identical to the built-in primid part (315 distinct, max 99) and ray:objectid is non-zero. Producer v1_q2_render.py cases bare_names / ray_names.
findings.reproduces: R101 — and strengthens it: the zero and non-zero cases occur in the same frame, which is the cleanest available control.

findings.claim: NEW MECHANISM, not recorded in R100-R106. The shipped default ID filter is UNSATISFIED on every render and falls back — and the fallback is what blends the mask boundary.
findings.anchor: Every successful render in this leg logged: "Pixel filter 'minmax' - Mode idcover requires PrimId channel" (v1_q2_render.json, all five successful cases). The default primidfilter/elementfilter is ["minmax",{"mode":"idcover"}] (v1_q2_parmdetail.json) — a coverage-based SELECTION filter that should never blend. Measured blending at 160x90: primid 583 of 14,400 px non-integral = 4.05%; element 993 = 6.90% (v1_q2_analysis.json integral_frac 0.9595 / 0.9310).
findings.relates_to: R100 / V1-F3 confirmed the blending; this supplies the cause.

findings.claim: Copernicus buffer readback is CONFIRMED, verified twice as the brief required, and it carries INTEGER storage. hou.CopNode.layer() -> hou.ImageLayer.allBufferElements(storagetype, channels) -> bytes.
findings.anchor: Verification 1 STRUCTURAL (v1_q1_cop_readback.json): all seven storage types return byte-exact lengths for 1024x1024x4 — Float32 and Int32 both 16,777,216 B; Float16/Int16/Fixed16 8,388,608 B; Int8/Fixed8 4,194,304 B; repeat_identical=true for all seven. Verification 2 CONTENT (v1_q1_cop_content_control.json): (a) driven value constant.f1=0.15 -> buffer (0.15,0.15,0.15,1.0) exact, bytes_changed=true; (b) fractalnoise -> 949,595 distinct values across 4,194,304 elements, min 0.179 max 1.000 — a fixed default cannot fake a gradient. Timing 2.4 ms median (min 2.367, max 7.197, 5 runs).
findings.reproduces: R102 — corroborated at a different resolution; 2.4 ms at 1024x1024 is consistent with R102's 7.74 ms at 1920x1080 by pixel count.
findings.note: The content check FIRST returned INCONCLUSIVE and said so — it filtered for parms named *color*, the constant COP names them f4r/f4g/f4b/f4a, and an all-1.0 buffer proves nothing. Diagnosis: under signature='auto' the node drives from the f1 branch. My error, not a readback defect, and recorded because the first status was wrong.

findings.claim: CORRECTION TO R102's positive control. hou.CopNode carries none of the legacy Cop2Node readback verbs — but 'getPixel' is ABSENT on hou.Cop2Node TOO, so it is not covered by the same-class control R102 cites.
findings.anchor: v1_q1_symbols.json: hou.CopNode (340 members) — allPixels/planes/getPixel/xRes/yRes/saveImage/layers/cookLayer/dataLayer all ABSENT. hou.Cop2Node (344 members) — allPixels/planes/xRes/yRes/saveImage CONFIRMED, getPixel ABSENT. The real legacy spellings are getPixelByUV / getPixelHSVByUV / getPixelLuminanceByUV (v1_q1_sweep.json class_hits['hou.Cop2Node']).
findings.disposition: Drop getPixel from R102's control list. It is an unspelled name, not a removed one — the same class of error R50 was written for.

findings.claim: retina/ingest.py selects the WRONG ID AOV on a real shipped Karma frame and REPORTS SUCCESS. find_id_subimage() returns 'element', not 'primid'; read_id_plane() then succeeds and hands back the element plane. Its own error message instructs the caller to set karmarendersettings.primid=1, and doing so does not make it read primid.
findings.anchor: RUN, not read — v1_q2_ingest_check.json: parts [0]C [1]element [2]primid; find_id_subimage -> 1 => 'element'; primid_part_index=2; selects_primid=false; read_id_plane ok, max 1228.75 (the element plane). Cause: ID_PART_NAMES=('primid','id','cryptomatte') substring-matches 'id' against CHANNEL name 'element.id' before reaching primid. retina/ingest.py:65 and :164, re-verified at commit 6983c73.
findings.bounded_by_control: R73 discipline. With element off, parts are [C, primid] and find_id_subimage returns the CORRECT index (v1_q3_cost_and_controls.json B_ingest_control.correct=true). The defect is CONDITIONAL on an earlier part whose part-or-channel name contains 'id' — element.id is the one that ships.
findings.why_untested: retina/tests/fixtures/exr_synth.py:multipart_exr_bytes builds exactly two parts, C + primid. The shadowing part is ABSENT from the fixture, so the ordering bug cannot fire in the suite. Law 1: the check cannot fail.
findings.out_of_fence: This is a product defect outside V1's read-only fence. Reported, not fixed.

findings.claim: The instrument is DETERMINISTIC. Two renders of the identical scene in SEPARATE husk processes produced pixel-identical output on every part. The sampling-noise floor on this path is ZERO — which contradicts a load-bearing premise of the harness that dispatched this leg.
findings.anchor: v1_q2_analysis.json base_vs_noise — C identical=true max_abs_diff=0.0; element identical=true 0.0; primid identical=true 0.0. Separate husk PIDs per case (v1_q2_render.json). The EXR FILES differ in byte length (36,876 vs 36,899) from metadata; the PIXELS do not differ at all.
findings.contradicts: SYNAPSE_RETINA_VERIFY.md §0: 'Two renders of the same scene differ — Monte Carlo. So delta > 0 means nothing.' On Karma CPU at fixed sampling, cross-process, that is false.
findings.scope_limit: One frame, one trivial scene, one machine, CPU engine, fixed sample counts, denoiser off. Stated as a strong prior for V2's control, NOT as an unconditional property.

findings.claim: The denoiser is controllable per-render and is OFF BY DEFAULT. Even when enabled it touches only the AOVs named in denoise_aovs (default 'C') and leaves the ID planes bit-identical.
findings.anchor: Declared: karmarendersettings.denoiser default 'off', menu ['off','optix','oidn']; denoise_aovs default 'C'; denoise_separate_aovs default False (v1_q2_parmdetail.json). MEASURED, not just declared: with denoiser='oidn', beauty C changed on 14.03% of pixels (max abs diff 0.1432) while element and primid were bit-identical, max abs diff 0.0 (v1_q2_analysis.json base_vs_denoise). Viewport-side control hou.GeometryViewportSettings.setUseDenoising / .useDenoising CONFIRMED as symbols (v1_q1_detail.json); Copernicus ships denoiseai and denoisetvd node types.

findings.claim: One capture costs ~2.4 s and the cost is FLAT IN RESOLUTION — it is husk process-spawn overhead, not pixels. 64x the pixels costs +12% wall-clock.
findings.anchor: v1_q3_cost_and_controls.json C_cost_curve: 160x90 2.239 s; 320x180 2.153 s; 640x360 2.217 s; 1280x720 2.502 s. Independently corroborated by the six-case matrix (v1_q2_render.json): 2.153-2.502 s across eleven renders. Command: usdrender_rop.render(verbose=False) under hython3.13, Karma CPU, samplesperpixel=4, pathtracedsamples=16, primid+element on, denoiser off.
findings.consequence: Capture at full resolution costs the same as at thumbnail. The design question is not what resolution is affordable but how often 2.4 s is affordable. Per-mutation verification sits at the expensive end of the brief's 0.4-vs-40-second framing.
findings.interruptibility: NOT interruptible from the calling thread. hou.RopNode has no cancel verb (V1-F14); hou.IPRViewer.killRender exists but requires a GUI.
findings.cheap_alternative: Copernicus readback of a full 1024x1024x4 float32 buffer: 2.4 ms median, in-process, no disk — roughly 1000x cheaper (V1-F7).

findings.claim: husk WORKS on Houdini Indie on 22.0.368. Eleven renders wrote real pixels to disk.
findings.anchor: hou.licenseCategory() = licenseCategoryType.Indie (v1_q1_symbols.json). Eleven EXRs written, 36,876-c.400,000 bytes, all readable by OIIO with correct part structure (v1_q2_render.json, v1_q3_cost_and_controls.json).
findings.supersedes: The standing H21 note that Houdini Indie silently no-ops husk (usdrender_rop.render() writes nothing). That was recorded on H21.0.671 and does NOT hold on 22.0.368. Stated as build-specific, not as a claim about Indie generally.

findings.claim: The GUI capture verbs EXIST as symbols and their BEHAVIOUR is UNVERIFIABLE headless. These are different claims and this leg does not merge them.
findings.anchor: CONFIRMED symbols (v1_q1_symbols.json, v1_q1_detail.json): hou.SceneViewer.flipbook(viewport, settings, open_dialog) and .flipbookSettings(); hou.FlipbookSettings 9/9 probed spellings incl. output/outputToMPlay/resolution/frameRange (82 members); hou.GeometryViewport._captureFramebuffer(buffer_name, filename); hou.IPRViewer.pixel/pixels/planes/saveFrame/killRender (104 members); hou.saveImageDataToFile(data,w,h,file,flip_vertical) writing .pic / 32-bit float RGBA only. ABSENT with same-class controls: hou.RopNode cancel/abort/interrupt/stop/kill/killRender (318 members, render+bypass resolve); hou.GeometryViewport saveViewToFile/flipbook/screenshot (93 members, saveViewToCamera+resolutionInPixels resolve); hou.ActiveRender / hou.activeRenders (853 top-level names). UNVERIFIABLE per R50/H3a-F5: hou.ui and hou.qt are absent from headless hython, so no SceneViewer or IPRViewer instance can be obtained — the verdict is UNVERIFIABLE, never ABSENT (v1_q3_cost_and_controls.json D_flipbook).
findings.reproduces: H3a-F1 / R58 / R73's NARROW claim — no cancel verb on hou.RopNode, and hou.ActiveRender genuinely absent.

findings.claim: CRYPTOMATTE IS UN-PROBED and it is the single highest-value remaining candidate for per-object identity. V2 should not be declared dead until it is run.
findings.anchor: The rendervar LOP carries a full cryptomatte parm group, dumped but not exercised: xn__driverparametersaovkarmacryptomatte_2xbkdf (toggle, default False), ...cryptomatterank_l4bkdf (default 6), ...cryptomattesidecar_h9bkdf (v1_q2_parmdetail.json rendervar_all_parms). retina/ingest.py already lists 'cryptomatte' in ID_PART_NAMES. Cryptomatte is DESIGNED to be a per-object matte; this leg tested primid, element and ray:objectid and did not test it.
findings.honesty: Recorded as a gap in THIS leg's coverage, not as a defect in the build. Naming it is cheaper than a V2 built on the assumption that every path was tried.

symbol_ledger.note: Full verdicts with dir() anchors in harness/notes/v1_q1_symbols.json (per-class) and v1_q1_sweep.json (namespace-wide). Every ABSENT below carries a same-class positive control (R50).
ABSENT: hou.RopNode.{cancel,abort,interrupt,stop,kill,killRender} — control: same class, 318 members, render+bypass resolve
hou.ActiveRender, hou.activeRenders — control: 853 top-level names, hou.hscript + hou.InterruptableOperation resolve

hou.CopNode.{allPixels,planes,getPixel,xRes,yRes,saveImage,layers,cookLayer,dataLayer} — control: allPixels/planes/xRes/yRes/saveImage resolve on hou.Cop2Node (344 members) in the same run; NOTE getPixel is absent there too (V1-F8)

INVOCABILITY of hou.SceneViewer.flipbook, hou.GeometryViewport._captureFramebuffer, hou.IPRViewer.* and hou.GeometryViewportSettings.setUseDenoising — all require a GUI; symbols CONFIRMED, behaviour untestable in this interpreter

did_not: substitute an assumed API for a refuted one
re-litigate the quarantined-absent list (hou.pdg.*, hou.secure, hou.lopNetworks(), hou.updateGraphTick())
scope_discipline.render_outputs: Eleven EXRs were written to the session scratchpad OUTSIDE the repo, deliberately, so no binaries entered the tree. Only scripts and JSON are in harness/notes/. Every render is reproducible by re-running the named producer.
scope_discipline.absence_as_deliverable: The brief says if a capability is absent, that absence IS the deliverable. V1-F1 through V1-F4 are that deliverable. No workaround was invented and no assumed API was substituted.

drift.note: V1 HAD ALREADY RUN, at 10:19 on 2026-07-27, and was ruled as R100-R106 (commit 098125f). Branch retina/v1-capture-probe is ZERO commits ahead of the line, its worktree is empty, and no V1.json and no probe script exist anywhere in the tree. R103 records the cause: the read-only fence denies Bash(git commit:*), so the product was never made durable and the worktree was later pruned. Consequence: every figure in R100-R106 — 7.74 ms, 50 ids with 49 shared, 7.4% of pixels — currently has NO producer path in the tree. That is a Law 2 violation created by the fence design, not by the agent. This run replaces those with reproducible producers and labels each result 'reproduces' or flags the difference.

THE LEG HAS NO WORKTREE AND THE TREE MOVED UNDER IT. legs.json declares worktree .claude/worktrees/v1-capture-probe; that directory is empty and is not a registered git worktree, so this leg ran against the shared main checkout. Mid-run a concurrent leg re-pointed that directory from feat/repair-heats-01 @ 2105453 to docs/how-we-know @ 6983c73. All Q1-Q4 findings are VERIFIED-RUNTIME against the live Houdini build and are unaffected; the one VERIFIED-STATIC finding (retina/ingest.py:65,:164) was re-verified against the new commit and holds. This is exactly the failure Constitution Article V's one-worktree-per-agent rule exists to prevent, and it is the same mechanism that lost the first V1's receipt.

The brief states 'R73 established the only render stop is rkill'. R73's own evidence table also lists hou.IPRViewer.killRender as PRESENT. Does not change V1's conclusions — killRender needs a GUI, so a headless capture remains uninterruptible.

for_ruling.question: V1 already ran and was ruled as R100-R106, but its receipt and producers are absent from the tree (drift D1). Does THIS receipt supersede R100-R106, annotate them as the surviving evidence, or sit beside them as an independent replication?
for_ruling.why_it_needs_a_human: Article I — this is a value judgement about the standing of an existing ruling block, not something provable from the tree.
for_ruling.evidence_offered: Every R100-R106 claim this leg re-tested was REPRODUCED. Two refinements are offered: V1-F6 supplies the mechanism behind R100-F3's blending, and V1-F8 corrects R102's positive-control list.

for_ruling.question: V1-F8: R102 licenses its hou.CopNode ABSENT verdicts by citing getPixel resolving on hou.Cop2Node. It does not resolve there either. Strike getPixel from R102's control list?
for_ruling.recommendation: Yes — the remaining four control spellings (allPixels, planes, xRes, saveImage) are verified and carry R102's conclusion unchanged. Only the control list is wrong, not the verdict.

for_ruling.question: V1-F15: cryptomatte is the one per-object-identity candidate this leg did NOT probe, and it is the mechanism actually designed for the job. Does a V1b run before V2-V4 are declared dead?
for_ruling.why_it_matters: R100 ruled V2-V4 'do not exist as designed' on the strength of primid/element/ray:objectid. That conclusion is correct for those three. Cryptomatte was not in the sample.

for_ruling.question: V1-F9: retina/ingest.py silently reads the wrong ID AOV and reports success, and the fixture cannot express the failure. Repair leg?
for_ruling.why_it_needs_a_human: It is a product defect outside V1's read-only fence. V1 reported rather than fixed, per the fence.
for_ruling.scope_note: The fix is two parts: (a) match the ID part by exact part name rather than substring, and (b) extend exr_synth.multipart_exr_bytes to emit a C+element+primid frame so the check CAN fail (Law 1).

for_ruling.question: V1-F10: SYNAPSE_RETINA_VERIFY.md §0 asserts renders of the same scene always differ, and V2 is designed around measuring that floor. On Karma CPU at fixed sampling the floor measured ZERO, cross-process. Does V2's design change?
for_ruling.recommendation: Do not weaken V2's control on this evidence. One trivial scene on one machine is a strong prior, not a licence — but V2 should now be able to state the condition under which the floor is non-zero, rather than assuming it always is.

for_ruling.question: Drift D1+D2: a read-only leg cannot commit, its declared worktree does not exist, and a concurrent leg can re-point the shared checkout under it. The first V1's evidence was lost to exactly this. Does the read-only profile gain a durability mechanism, or does legs.json stop declaring worktrees that are never created?
for_ruling.why_it_needs_a_human: Article I gate — it is a change to the fence, and Article I says an agent may not edit its own leash. Recorded here rather than acted on.
